Standard: Flight performance of refueling equipment is assessed as no worse than 6 from MIL- STD-1797, Cooper-Harper pilot rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system) and has satisfactory workload (if applicable) to allow AR operations with targeted receiver air vehicles. a. Boom Tanker. Boom system flight performance is assessed as no worse than 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper pilot rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system) and has satisfactory workload when operated in proximity to receiver air vehicles. Boom flying qualities, response, stability and control, control sensitivity, time delay, oscillations, undesirable motions, workload and handling qualities are no worse than 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper pilot rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system) for refueling tasks. b. Drogue Tanker. Hose and drogue are stable during extension, retraction, and at full trail throughout the AR envelope. Hose reel system provides catenary curve and drogue presentation angle which permit probe engagement throughout refueling envelope. In free air, disturbances of the refueling hose damp-out to one-third amplitude in three cycles and disturbances of the drogue damp-out to one-half drogue diameter. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Computational modeling and analysis of boom flight control laws predict boom will meet required levels of controllability in proximity to receiver air vehicles. Modeling shows excitation disturbances of the boom damp-out. b. Drogue Tanker. Analysis shows hose and drogue are stable in trail throughout refueling envelope, catenary curve and drogue presentation angle permit probe engagement throughout refueling envelope. Modeling of hose and drogue show disturbances and excitations damp-out. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. 1. Wind tunnel testing verifies aerodynamic performance matches analytical values and shows boom is stable in the expected airflow environment and disturbances damp-out as required. 2. Ground based simulation and SIL testing with operator in the loop shows the boom is stable and controllable throughout the expected airspeed and altitude envelope to the extents of the boom control envelope. b. Drogue Tanker. Wind tunnel testing of trailing components verifies disturbances of the hose and drogue damp-out as required and the catenary curve and drogue presentation angle permits probe engagement. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight evaluations of boom performance during free air flight and AR operation, including predictability of response, stability and control, control sensitivity, tactile feedback, time delay, oscillations, PIO tendencies, undesirable motions, workload and handling qualities verify boom flight performance is assessed as no worse than 6 from MIL-STD-1797, Cooper-Harper pilot rating scale figure (or equivalent rating system). Test points include, free air maneuvering, receptacle tracking, contacts and disconnects, in straight and level flight, turns, and toboggans, with targeted receiver air vehicles, throughout the AR envelope at the extremes of the boom disconnect envelope, at worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs. b. Drogue Tanker. 1. Flight testing verifies hose and drogue are stable and can be trailed, rewound and stowed throughout the refueling envelope. 2. Flight testing verifies hose reel system provides catenary curve and drogue presentation angle which permits probe engagement throughout refueling envelope. 3. Flight testing verifies, in free air, disturbances of the hose damp-out to one-third amplitude in three cycles and disturbances of the drogue damp-out to one-half diameter.
